name: Grapes and raisins
note: In dogs, grapes and raisins can cause kidney failure even in small amounts (ASPCA). Published guidance focuses on dogs; if a cat ate any, call your vet.

name: Chocolate and cocoa
note: Chocolate, coffee and caffeine contain methylxanthines. Darker chocolate and cocoa powder are more dangerous (ASPCA).

name: Onion, garlic and leek
note: Allium plants (onion, garlic, chives, leek) can damage red blood cells. Cats are more susceptible; dogs are also at risk (ASPCA).

name: Xylitol (sweetener)
note: Xylitol in gum, candy and baked goods can cause a sharp drop in blood sugar and liver damage in dogs (ASPCA). Evidence for cats is limited; still avoid sharing.

name: Cooked chicken (plain)
note: Plain cooked chicken without bones, seasoning, onion or garlic is a common safe treat. Raw chicken can carry bacteria (ASPCA).

name: Carrot
note: Carrot is not on the ASPCA people-foods-to-avoid list. Offer in small pieces to reduce choking risk.
